questions.question: In which month was the Economic Survey 2024–25 presented?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**January 2025**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Economic Survey 2024-25** is a flagship annual document of the **Ministry of Finance**, Government of India. It is traditionally presented in **Parliament** during the **Budget Session**, usually on **January 31st**, which falls in the month of **January 2025**.
 
• It is presented by the **Union Finance Minister** (currently **Nirmala Sitharaman**) in both the **Lok Sabha** and the **Rajya Sabha**. The presentation occurs exactly one day before the **Union Budget** is introduced.
 
• The document is prepared by the **Economics Division** of the **Department of Economic Affairs** (DEA) under the comprehensive guidance of the **Chief Economic Advisor** (CEA), currently **V. Anantha Nageswaran**.
 
• The **Economic Survey** serves as an official report card of the **Indian Economy** for the preceding financial year, detailing the performance of various sectors and the overall **macroeconomic** health of the nation.
 
• Since the **Union Budget 2025-26** is scheduled for **February 1, 2025**, the preceding **Economic Survey** for the fiscal year **2024-25** is presented in **January 2025** to provide the necessary context for the upcoming budget's proposals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Historical Context of the Survey**:
 
 
• The first **Economic Survey** of India was presented in the year **1950-51**.
 
• Up until **1964**, the survey was presented along with the **Union Budget**. However, from **1964** onwards, it was decoupled and presented a day earlier to allow for a better understanding of the budget's background.
 
 
 
• **Growth Projections and GDP**:
 
 
• The survey provides **GDP growth** projections for the upcoming fiscal year. For **2024-25**, it analyzes factors like **inflation**, **fiscal deficit**, and **current account deficit**.
 
• It helps the **Government of India** and the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** in formulating **monetary** and **fiscal policies** based on the data of the **National Statistical Office (NSO)**.
 
 
 
• **Key Sectoral Analysis**:
 
 
• The document provides detailed chapters on the **Agricultural Sector**, **Industrial Sector**, and **Services Sector**.
 
• It also focuses on **Foreign Exchange Reserves**, **Export-Import (EXIM)** trends, and **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Constitutional Status**: While the **Union Budget** is a constitutional requirement under **Article 112** (referred to as the **Annual Financial Statement**), the **Economic Survey** is not mandated by the **Constitution of India**. It is a settled convention that has become an integral part of the budget process.
 
• **Interim Budget Exception**: In an **Election Year** (such as **2024**), the government may present an **Interim Budget** in February and a full budget along with the **Economic Survey** later in the year after the new government is formed. However, for a regular cycle like **2024-25** leading into **2025-26**, the **January** presentation remains standard.
 
• **Significance for Stakeholders**: The survey is highly anticipated by **economists**, **investors**, and **policymakers** as it highlights the **reforms** needed and the challenges facing the **Indian economy** in the global context.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following was rated as 'Good' by the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) in its global review of Natural World Heritage Sites in November 2025?

options.text: Nanda Devi and Valley of Flowers National Parks
Great Himalayan National Park Conservation Area

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Khangchendzonga National Park**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• In the global review conducted by the **International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN)** in **November 2025**, **Khangchendzonga National Park** was rated as **'Good'**. This rating signifies that the site's **World Heritage values** are well-protected and the management system is highly effective. 
• The **IUCN World Heritage Outlook** is a flagship report released every **three years** that tracks whether the conservation of natural **World Heritage sites** is sufficient to protect them in the long term. 
• **Khangchendzonga National Park**, situated in the heart of the **Himalayas** in **Sikkim**, is India’s first and only **'Mixed' World Heritage Site**, recognized for both its **natural** and **cultural** significance since **2016**. 
• The 'Good' rating highlights the park's success in maintaining its unique **high-altitude ecosystem** and protecting rare species despite the challenges posed by **climate change**. ***Hence, the correct answer is Khangchendzonga National Park.*** 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Khangchendzonga National Park (KNP):** 
• Located in the state of **Sikkim**, it includes a unique diversity of plains, valleys, lakes, glaciers, and spectacular snow-capped mountains covered with ancient forests. 
• It is home to **Mount Khangchendzonga**, the **third-highest peak** in the world. 
• The park provides a habitat for several endangered species, including the **Snow Leopard**, **Red Panda**, **Himalayan Black Bear**, and the **Tibetan Wolf**. 
• **Sundarbans National Park:** 
• Located in **West Bengal**, it is the world's largest **mangrove forest**. 
• It is often categorized under '**Significant Concern**' by the **IUCN** due to the rising sea levels and the high frequency of **cyclones** in the region. 
• **Great Himalayan National Park Conservation Area (GHNPCA):** 
• Located in **Kullu**, **Himachal Pradesh**, it was inscribed on the **World Heritage List** in **2014**. 
• It is characterized by high alpine peaks, alpine meadows, and riverine forests. 
• **Nanda Devi and Valley of Flowers National Parks:** 
• Located in **Uttarakhand**, these parks are renowned for their meadows of endemic alpine flowers and outstanding natural beauty. 
• **Nanda Devi National Park** was inscribed in **1988**, and the **Valley of Flowers** was added to the site in **2005**. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• The **IUCN** uses four categories to rate sites: **Good**, **Good with Some Concern**, **Significant Concern**, and **Critical**. 
• The **International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN)** was established in **1948** and is headquartered in **Gland, Switzerland**. It serves as the official advisory body on nature to the **UNESCO World Heritage Committee**. 
• As of **2025**, the major threats identified for Indian natural heritage sites include **invasive species**, **climate change**, and **infrastructure development**.

questions.question: Which individual, celebrated as India's first Paralympic gold medalist, was honoured with the Arjuna Lifetime Achievement Award in January 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Murlikant Petkar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Murlikant Petkar** was conferred with the prestigious **Arjuna Lifetime Achievement Award** in **January 2025** in recognition of his pioneering contributions to Indian sports.
 
• He holds the distinction of being **India's first Paralympic gold medalist**, a feat he achieved more than five decades ago.
 
• His historic **gold medal** was won at the **1972 Summer Paralympics** held in **Heidelberg, West Germany**.
 
• He competed in the **50m Freestyle swimming** event, where he set a **World Record** at the time with a finish of **37.33 seconds**.
 
• The award presented in **2025** serves to honor his legacy as the person who put India on the **Paralympic** map long before the nation became a regular contender for medals in the event.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Military Career and Injury:**
 
 
• Before becoming an athlete, Petkar was a soldier in the **Indian Army**, serving in the **Corps of Electronics and Mechanical Engineers (EME)**.
 
• He sustained severe injuries, including **nine bullet wounds**, during the **1965 Indo-Pak War** in the **Sialkot sector**, which led to him becoming paraplegic.
 
 
 
• **Multifaceted Athlete:**
 
 
• Petkar was a versatile sportsman; he initially represented India in **Table Tennis** at the **1968 Tel Aviv Paralympics**.
 
• Apart from swimming, he has also competed internationally in **Javelin Throw**, **Precision Javelin Throw**, and **Shot Put**.
 
 
 
• **National Honors:**
 
 
• He was awarded the **Padma Shri**, India's fourth-highest civilian award, in **2018** by the **Government of India**.
 
• His life story was the inspiration for the **2024 biographical film** titled **"Chandu Champion"**, directed by **Kabir Khan** and starring **Kartik Aaryan**.
 
 
 
• **Evolution of Awards:**
 
 
• The **Arjuna Award** is usually given for outstanding performance over the previous **four years**, but the **Lifetime Achievement** category recognizes legends whose impact spans decades.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Devendra Jhajharia:** He is another legendary para-athlete who won **two gold medals** in **Javelin Throw** (**2004 Athens** and **2016 Rio**) and served as a major inspiration for the current generation.
 
• **Mariyappan Thangavelu:** He won the **gold medal** in the **Men's High Jump T42** category at the **2016 Rio Paralympics**.
 
• **Deepa Malik:** She was the **first Indian woman** to win a **Paralympic medal**, securing a **silver** in **Shot Put** at the **2016 Rio Games**.
 
• **Significance of 1972:** Petkar's gold in **1972** was India's only individual **Olympic** or **Paralympic** gold until **Abhinav Bindra** won gold in **2008** and **Devendra Jhajharia** won in **2004**.
</ul

questions.question: International Women’s Day, a global day celebrating the social, economic, cultural and political achievements of women, is celebrated on which of the following dates?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**8 March**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **International Women’s Day (IWD)** is celebrated annually on **8 March** to recognize the social, economic, cultural, and political achievements of women worldwide.
 
• The day also marks a call to action for accelerating **gender parity** and raising awareness about women's equality.
 
• The first **National Woman's Day** was observed in the **United States** on **February 28, 1909**, organized by the **Socialist Party of America**.
 
• The idea to make the day international was proposed by **Clara Zetkin** at the **International Conference of Working Women** in **Copenhagen** in **1910**.
 
• As a result of the Copenhagen initiative, **International Women’s Day** was honored for the first time in **Austria**, **Denmark**, **Germany**, and **Switzerland** on **19 March 1911**.
 
• The date of **8 March** became fixed after women in **Russia** gained the right to vote following a strike for "Bread and Peace" in **1917**, which began on **8 March** (Gregorian calendar).
 
• The **United Nations** began celebrating International Women's Day in **1975**, which was designated as **International Women's Year**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **16 June:**
 
 
• This date is observed as the **International Day of the African Child**.
 
• It commemorates the **1976 Soweto Uprising** in **South Africa**, where thousands of black school children protested against the poor quality of their education and demanded the right to be taught in their own language.
 
• It is also celebrated as **Youth Day** in **South Africa** to honor the students who lost their lives during the protest.
 
 
 
• **20 November:**
 
 
• This date is recognized as **World Children's Day** (or Universal Children's Day).
 
• It marks the anniversary of the date in **1959** when the **UN General Assembly** adopted the **Declaration of the Rights of the Child**.
 
• It is also the date in **1989** when the UN General Assembly adopted the **Convention on the Rights of the Child**.
 
 
 
• **21 September:**
 
 
• This date is observed as the **International Day of Peace** (World Peace Day).
 
• Established in **1981** by the **United Nations**, it is dedicated to world peace and specifically the absence of war and violence.
 
• The **United Nations Peace Bell** is rung at **UN Headquarters** in **New York City** to inaugurate the day.
 
 
 
• **IWD Symbolism and Colors:**
 
 
• The official colors of **International Women's Day** are **Purple**, **Green**, and **White**.
 
• **Purple** signifies justice and dignity; **Green** symbolizes hope; and **White** represents purity (though purity is a controversial concept, it was originally used by the **Women's Social and Political Union** in the **UK**).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• In **1977**, the **United Nations General Assembly** invited member states to proclaim **March 8** as the **UN Day for women's rights and world peace**.
 
• Each year, the **United Nations** assigns a specific theme to the day. For example, the theme for **2024** was **'Invest in women: Accelerate progress'**.
 
• International Women's Day is an official holiday in many countries, including **Afghanistan**, **Armenia**, **Azerbaijan**, **Belarus**, **Cambodia**, **Cuba**, **Georgia**, **Laos**, **Mongolia**, **Montenegro**, **Russia**, **Tajikistan**, **Turkmenistan**, **Uganda**, **Ukraine**, **Uzbekistan**, **Vietnam**, and **Zambia**.
</ul

questions.question: Who was appointed as the Chairman of the Economic Advisory Council to the PM in June 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mahendra Dev**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mahendra Dev** was appointed as the **Chairman** of the **Economic Advisory Council to the Prime Minister (EAC-PM)** in **June 2025**.
 
• The **Economic Advisory Council to the Prime Minister (EAC-PM)** is an **independent body** constituted to provide **expert advice** on **economic** and related issues to the **Prime Minister of India**.
 
• Prior to this prestigious appointment, **Mahendra Dev** served as the **Director and Vice-Chancellor** of the **Indira Gandhi Institute of Development Research (IGIDR)** in **Mumbai**.
 
• He has also served as the **Chairman** of the **Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices (CACP)**, which is under the **Ministry of Agriculture**.
 
• His expertise spans **development economics**, **agricultural policy**, and **poverty alleviation**, making him a critical figure in shaping **India's macroeconomic strategy** for the mid-2020s.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Economic Advisory Council to the Prime Minister (EAC-PM):**
 
 
• It is a **non-constitutional**, **non-permanent**, and **non-statutory** body.
 
• The **Council** is tasked with analyzing any issue, economic or otherwise, referred to it by the **Prime Minister**.
 
• It maintains its secretariat within the **NITI Aayog** for **administrative** and **logistical support**.
 
 
 
• **Other Economists in the Options:**
 
 
• **Poonam Gupta**: She is the first female **Director General** of the **National Council of Applied Economic Research (NCAER)** and has been a **member** of the **EAC-PM**.
 
• **Arvind Subramanian**: A world-renowned economist who served as the **Chief Economic Adviser (CEA)** to the **Government of India** from **2014 to 2018**.
 
• **Vijay Kelkar**: A veteran economist and **civil servant** who served as the **Chairman** of the **13th Finance Commission** and is known for the **Kelkar Committee** reports on **tax reforms** and **PPP models**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Chairman** of the **EAC-PM** usually holds a rank equivalent to a **Cabinet Minister** in the **Union Government**.
 
• The **EAC-PM** has been instrumental in publishing major reports such as the **Competitiveness Roadmap for India@100** and the **State of Inequality in India Report**.
 
• The council typically consists of **full-time members** and **part-time members** who are experts from **academia** and the **private sector**.
 
• The terms of reference for the **EAC-PM** include addressing **macroeconomic issues**, **inflation**, **employment**, and **financial sector** stability.
</ul

questions.question: What was the cause of the warehouse explosion in Gujarat in April 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Aluminium powder explosion**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The tragic warehouse incident occurred in **April 2025** in the state of **Gujarat**, which is a major industrial and chemical hub in **India**.
 
• Preliminary investigations and forensic reports identified that the root cause of the blast was an **Aluminium powder explosion**, categorized as a high-intensity **dust explosion**.
 
• **Aluminium powder** is extremely **combustible** and reactive; when it is finely divided, it has a very high surface-area-to-volume ratio, making it prone to rapid **oxidation** and ignition if suspended in the air.
 
• The explosion likely occurred due to the accumulation of **metallic dust** in a confined space, where a small spark or heat source triggered a **primary explosion**, followed by a more devastating **secondary explosion** as settled dust was lofted into the atmosphere.
 
• Industrial safety experts noted that **Gujarat** hosts numerous units involved in **pigment manufacturing**, **pyrotechnics**, and **metallurgy**, where such hazardous materials are commonly stored. ***Hence, the correct answer is Aluminium powder explosion.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Properties of Aluminium Powder:**
 
 
• It is a **silvery-white** powder used extensively in **paints**, **explosives**, **rocket fuel**, and **solar cell** manufacturing.
 
• In its powder form, aluminium reacts with **oxygen** and **water** (releasing **hydrogen gas**), which can create a pressurized and highly flammable environment in sealed containers.
 
 
 
• **Combustible Dust Hazards:**
 
 
• A **dust explosion** requires five elements: **fuel** (dust), **dispersion**, **confinement**, **oxidizer** (oxygen), and an **ignition source**.
 
• Unlike liquid fires, **metal fires** (Class D) cannot be extinguished with water, as water can exacerbate the reaction by producing **hydrogen**.
 
 
 
• **Industrial Landscape of Gujarat:**
 
 
• **Gujarat** contributes significantly to **India's** industrial output, particularly in the **chemical and petrochemical** sectors.
 
• Major industrial zones like **Vapi**, **Ankleshwar**, and **Dahej** are strictly monitored under the **Factories Act, 1948**, to prevent such catastrophic failures.
 
 
 
• **Regulatory Framework:**
 
 
• The **Petroleum and Explosives Safety Organization (PESO)** is the nodal agency in **India** for regulating hazardous substances under the **Explosives Act, 1884**.
 
• Companies are required to maintain a **Material Safety Data Sheet (MSDS)** for all reactive chemicals to ensure workers are aware of **storage protocols** and **emergency response** steps.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Prevention and Mitigation:**
 
 
• Warehouses dealing with **Aluminium powder** must utilize **explosion-proof** lighting and **non-sparking** tools to minimize ignition risks.
 
• Effective **ventilation systems** and **dust extraction** units are mandatory to keep the concentration of airborne particles below the **Lower Explosive Limit (LEL)**.
 
• Regular **safety audits** and **mock drills** are emphasized by the **National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA)** to improve resilience against industrial disasters in high-risk zones.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: Which of these ISRO-led national initiatives, launched in July 2025, exemplifies international scientific collaboration while strengthening India’s Earth-observation and monitoring capabilities?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**NISAR**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **NISAR** (NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar) is a joint Earth-observation mission between the **National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA)** of the **United States** and the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)**.
 
• Scheduled for launch in **2025** (specifically targeted around **July 2025** as per mission updates), this initiative stands as a premier example of **international scientific collaboration** in space exploration.
 
• The mission aims to provide a detailed view of Earth using **Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR)** technology, which can observe the planet's surface in all weather conditions, day and night.
 
• It is the first satellite mission to use two different radar frequencies: the **L-band** (provided by **NASA**) and the **S-band** (provided by **ISRO**), allowing for high-resolution mapping of **ecosystems** and **ice mass**.
 
• The satellite will map the entire globe every **12 days**, providing spatially and temporally consistent data for understanding changes in **Earth’s ecosystems**, **ice sheets**, and **natural hazards**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mission Objectives and Applications:**
 
 
• The primary goal of **NISAR** is to measure **Earth’s changing ecosystems**, dynamic surfaces, and ice masses, offering insights into **biomass**, **natural hazards**, and **groundwater**.
 
• It will monitor **crustal deformation** caused by **earthquakes**, **volcanoes**, and **landslides**, helping in disaster management and risk assessment.
 
• The data will assist in tracking **sea level rise** and the rate of **glacier** melting in the **Arctic** and **Antarctic** regions.
 
 
 
• **Technical Contributions:**
 
 
• **ISRO** is responsible for providing the **S-band radar**, the spacecraft bus, and the launch services using the **GSLV Mark II** (Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle).
 
• **NASA** provides the **L-band SAR**, a high-rate communication subsystem for science data, **GPS receivers**, and a solid-state recorder.
 
• The **L-band SAR** has a wavelength of about **24 centimeters**, while the **S-band SAR** has a wavelength of about **10 centimeters**, making them ideal for different types of surface penetration and sensitivity.
 
 
 
• **Other Mentioned Initiatives:**
 
 
• **Gaganyaan**: India’s first **human spaceflight mission**, which aims to demonstrate indigenous capability by sending a crew of three members to an orbit of **400 km** for a 3-day mission.
 
• **Aditya-L1/L2**: **Aditya-L1** was launched in **September 2023** as India’s first dedicated mission to study the **Sun** from the Lagrange point 1. **Aditya-L2** is a conceptualized follow-up mission.
 
• **GSAT-12**: A **communication satellite** launched by **ISRO** in **July 2011** to provide services like tele-education, tele-medicine, and Village Resource Centres.
 
 
 
• **Global Impact:**
 
 
• The **NISAR** mission data will be **open-access**, supporting the global scientific community in **climate change** research and sustainable **agriculture**.
 
• It represents a strategic partnership signed in **2014**, showcasing the growing **Indo-US space cooperation**.
 
 

67

questions.question: Which of the following legislations was approved by the Rajya Sabha on 12 August 2025, aiming to recognise national sports organisations and oversee their operations?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**National Sports Governance Bill, 2025**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **National Sports Governance Bill, 2025** was approved by the **Rajya Sabha** on **12 August 2025**. This legislation marks a significant shift in how sports are administered in the country by providing a **statutory framework** for the recognition and regulation of sports bodies.
 
• The primary objective of the bill is to **recognize national sports organisations** (NSOs) and **oversee their operations** to ensure they adhere to principles of **transparency** and **accountability**.
 
• Under this Act, the **Central Government** is empowered to grant recognition to **National Sports Federations (NSFs)** and the **Indian Olympic Association (IOA)**, provided they comply with the prescribed governance standards. ***Hence, the bill aims to streamline the functioning of these bodies.***
 
• The bill introduces a **National Sports Regulatory Board**, which will act as an apex body to monitor the compliance of various sports organizations with the new **National Sports Code**.
 
• It emphasizes **athlete-centric administration**, ensuring that the interests of sportspersons are prioritized over administrative bureaucracy in **National Sports Organisations**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Regulatory Framework:** Before this bill, sports governance was largely guided by the **National Sports Development Code of India, 2011**. The **2025 Bill** codifies many of these guidelines into law, making them legally binding on all recognized sports entities.
 
• **Dispute Resolution:** The bill proposes the establishment of a **National Sports Dispute Resolution and Appellate Tribunal**.
